key_insight: A local, scale-invariant subfilter wave drag model in LES shows that ocean-wave properties can significantly alter air-sea momentum flux, not just near-surface wind speed.
engineering_relevance: Accurately representing wave–turbulence coupling is important for climate prediction, offshore wind design, ocean circulation modeling, and marine engineering.
method: Large Eddy Simulation of the marine atmospheric boundary layer (MABL).
Introduced a local subfilter wave drag parameterization for dynamic, unresolved wave effects.
Varied significant wave height and peak spectral frequency to assess momentum-flux sensitivity.
evidence_signal: Model results were compared against field data and used to examine how friction velocity and surface stress depend on both wind and wave conditions.
watch_item: The approach may be sensitive to how wave spectra and subfilter drag are parameterized, so transferability across sea states and resolutions should be checked carefully.
paper_title: Sea Surface Roughness Dependence on Ocean Wave Parameters through Large Eddy Simulation with Local Subfilter Wave Drag
